name: Bridesmaid's Cake
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: little rose water and mace
ingredients.originalText: A little rose water and mace

instructions.text: Butter and sugar beaten to a cream, the whites of eggs beaten to a stiff froth, almonds pounded fine, with rose water and sherry, and a little mace, are made into a paste; rub this into three-quarter pounds of flour, and add lightly and quickly to the other ingredients already mixed.
The almonds, paste, and flour should be prepared first.

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Butter and sugar beaten to a cream, the whites of eggs beaten to a stiff froth, almonds pounded fine, with rose water and sherry, and a little mace, are made into a paste; rub this into three-quarter pounds of flour, and add lightly and quickly to the other ingredients already mixed.
2. The almonds, paste, and flour should be prepared first.
3. Bake in moderate oven.
